questions.question: Your manager wants to see how one branch's sales moved across the 12 months of the year. Which chart suits this best?

answerOptions.text: Line chart
answerOptions.rationale: A line shows a trend over time, which is exactly the question.

answerOptions.text: Pie chart
answerOptions.rationale: A pie shows share of a whole, not change over time.

answerOptions.text: Histogram
answerOptions.rationale: A histogram shows how values are spread across bins, not a monthly trend.

answerOptions.text: Treemap
answerOptions.rationale: A treemap shows share within categories, not movement over months.

questions.question: You select A1:E14 for a column chart, including the Total row. What goes wrong?

answerOptions.text: Excel refuses to chart any row labelled Total
answerOptions.rationale: Excel charts it happily; the problem is the scale, not an error.

answerOptions.text: The chart switches to a pie chart automatically
answerOptions.rationale: Excel keeps the chart type you picked.

answerOptions.text: The Total bars tower over the months and squash the monthly bars flat
answerOptions.rationale: A total is far bigger than its parts, so never chart a total with its parts.

answerOptions.text: Switch Row/Column stops working on that chart
answerOptions.rationale: Switch Row/Column still works; the Total bars are the real issue.

questions.question: To highlight one product's bar, the helper column uses =IF(A2=$F$1,B2,NA()). Why NA() for the other rows?

answerOptions.text: NA() tells Excel to colour those bars grey
answerOptions.rationale: NA() returns an error value; it does not set any colour.

answerOptions.text: A chart does not draw #N/A, so the helper series shows only the matching bar
answerOptions.rationale: The helper draws one bar, which is laid on top of the original with 100% overlap.

answerOptions.text: NA() hides those rows from the worksheet
answerOptions.rationale: The rows stay visible; only the chart skips the #N/A points.

answerOptions.text: NA() is required because IF cannot return a number
answerOptions.rationale: IF can return numbers; NA() is chosen because charts skip it.

questions.question: On a column chart of monthly sales in rupees, you add a monthly sales target, also in rupees, as a line. How should you set it up?

answerOptions.text: Put Target on a secondary axis so it stands out
answerOptions.rationale: A target on its own axis floats at the wrong height against the bars.

answerOptions.text: Stack the Target on top of the sales columns
answerOptions.rationale: Stacking adds the target to sales, which gives a meaningless total.

answerOptions.text: Show the target as a separate pie chart
answerOptions.rationale: A pie shows share, not a comparison with monthly sales.

answerOptions.text: Make Target a line on the main axis, with Secondary Axis unticked
answerOptions.rationale: Target and sales share the same rupee units, so they share one axis.

questions.question: In your profit bridge waterfall, Gross profit floats in mid-air like another increase. What is the fix?

answerOptions.text: Type Gross profit as a negative number
answerOptions.rationale: Only costs go in as negatives; a subtotal is a SUM formula.

answerOptions.text: Change the chart to a stacked column chart
answerOptions.rationale: That loses the step-up, step-down bridge you wanted.

answerOptions.text: Sort the data from largest to smallest
answerOptions.rationale: A bridge must follow the order of the profit statement.

answerOptions.text: Select that bar and tick Set as total in the Format pane
answerOptions.rationale: Set as total makes the subtotal start from zero on the axis.

questions.question: You want one box-and-whisker box per region, but you get a single box for the whole company. What did you miss?

answerOptions.text: Setting the bin width to 5,000
answerOptions.rationale: Bin width belongs to histograms, not box plots.

answerOptions.text: Selecting the Region column together with the order values
answerOptions.rationale: With region and value selected together, Excel draws one box per region.

answerOptions.text: Sorting the order values largest first
answerOptions.rationale: Sorting does not split the data into groups.

answerOptions.text: Choosing the Pareto option
answerOptions.rationale: Pareto draws sorted bars with a cumulative line, not boxes.

questions.question: Your India map chart leaves Odisha unshaded because the data says Orissa. What is the right fix?

answerOptions.text: Set Map area to Only regions with data
answerOptions.rationale: That only zooms the map; it does not fix an unmatched name.

answerOptions.text: Remove the Country column so Excel searches more widely
answerOptions.rationale: The Country = India column prevents wrong matches, so keep it.

answerOptions.text: Change the name in the data to the official name, Odisha
answerOptions.rationale: Official state names match best when Excel looks up places through Bing.

answerOptions.text: Switch the chart to a sunburst
answerOptions.rationale: A sunburst does not show geography at all.

questions.question: Line sparklines for eight branches make a small branch swing as much as a big one. How do you make them comparable?

answerOptions.text: Sparkline tab > Axis > Same for All Sparklines, for both minimum and maximum
answerOptions.rationale: One shared scale makes the lines fair to compare.

answerOptions.text: Tick High Point and Low Point
answerOptions.rationale: Markers show each line's best and worst month but keep separate scales.

answerOptions.text: Change them to Win/Loss sparklines
answerOptions.rationale: Win/Loss only shows above or below zero, not size.

answerOptions.text: Widen column N
answerOptions.rationale: A wider cell stretches the lines but does not change their scales.
